analysis: Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md, a developer testing guide (lines 1751-2704). No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing logic changes are visible in these excerpts, so no security regression appears. The content describes test procedures: Go/Rust prompt-sidecar preload tests, real-sidecar pairing with binary hash binding (lines 1789-1811), MiMo fixtures, provider CI lanes, coverage reporting, doctor/statusCanonical vectors (lines 2550-2568), and SSD cache tests (tamperFailsClosed, lines 2166-2189). The docs say tests use temporary files, in-memory keys and sanitized environments and need no production credentials. Test guidance states SSD tests do not exercise a hardware-backed key, and that Rust and Go tests do not establish native KV adoption. This is consistent with T-041 and does not alter its posture: the HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL and AES-GCM tamper rejection are unchanged. Unverified: the patch hunks were not supplied, only head text, so I cannot tell which doc lines changed. Referenced test files and scripts were not inspected. The excerpts do not change the threat model's assumptions for TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. The next pass should check that any non-doc files in the PR are consistent with these docs. I treat the docs as untrusted evidence.
